title: Past Perfect Basics

vocab.ex: I realised I had left my phone at home.
She had warned me about the traffic.
The past perfect describes the earlier action.
The past simple describes the later action.
They had already left.
She hadn't eaten before the meeting.
Past Perfect helps show the sequence of events.
I had studied before the test.
She called after she had left.
By the time I arrived, they had left.
They had already decided.
I had just finished when she called.
I felt relieved when I saw she had arrived.
These are two past actions in order.
The first thing that happened was the delay.
The second thing that happened was our arrival.
The previous flight had been cancelled.
Prior to the meeting, I had read the report.
The background story used Past Perfect.
The flashback showed what had happened before.
I had finished before she arrived.
They had left when I called.
She had already decided before we talked.
We had eaten before the movie started.
The shop had closed by the time we got there.
She had arrived before the storm started.
He had lost his keys before he noticed.
I had forgotten her name by the next day.
They had planned the trip months before.
She had realized her mistake before I said anything.

expressions.example: By the time I arrived, they had already left.
I had already decided before she called.
She had never seen snow before that trip.
After I had finished, I went for a walk.

grammar.title: Past Perfect: had + particípio passado
rules: Estrutura: had + particípio passado — HAD nunca muda, para nenhum sujeito.
Pergunta: Had + sujeito + particípio?: "Had you decided?"
Use para a ação que aconteceu PRIMEIRO, quando há duas ações no passado: "When I arrived (2ª), they had left (1ª)."

quiz.q: By the time I arrived, they ___ (leave).
